steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Latin verbs are conjugated (change form) to show person (1st, 2nd, 3rd), number (singular, plural), tense (when), voice (active/passive), and mood (indicative/subjunctive). | Key Fact: There are four conjugations, identified by the characteristic vowel in the present stem: 1st (-a-), 2nd (-e-), 3rd (short -e- or consonant), 4th (-i-). | Key Fact: Every Latin verb has four principal parts that must be memorised: e.g. laudo, laudare, laudavi, laudatus (I praise, to praise, I praised, praised). | Key Fact: Present tense personal endings: -o/m (I), -s (you), -t (he/she/it), -mus (we), -tis (you pl.), -nt (they).
